clues.title: Sign: Black sock sign post
text: White signposts painted black at the bottom are very common in both Russia and Kazakhstan. However, Kazakhstan's entire coverage was done with a pickup truck, making it easy to rule out, indicating you're in Russia.

clues.title: Pedestrian sign: Pedestrian Signs
text: Russian pedestrian signs have a simply drawn person and three stripes.
Signs will commonly have a bright yellow border.
Ukraine, Lithuania, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan use the same design.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Wide Intersections
text: Along with containing a large number of bollards, many intersections are unusually wide compared to other countries.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Gen 3 Cars
text: Three Generation 3 Street View cars are commonly found in Russia.
The two most useful ones for recognising Russia are a black and a white car, both with a long antenna.
You may also see a short antenna without a visible car.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Bollard: Bollards
text: **Russia has three main types of bollards:**
A very thin type being attached to a stick.
One with a black top section.
A red vertical reflector below and a German-style bollard.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Architecture: Large Apartments

Newer buildings in wealthier areas appear more modern.

clues.title: Landscape: Altai Mountains
text: The main road of Altai Republic has a black car long antenna driving north through the Altai Mountains, often with foggy or rainy coverage.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Buryatia
text: The landscape in Buryatia is very unique, containing open grassy landscape with shrubs and mountains. It is lusher near Baikal, but the mountains persist.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Google car: Caspian Sea Desert
text: In the desert-like region west of the Caspian Sea, this completely flat and rural Generation 4 coverage on small poorly-tracked dirt roads can only be found in northern Dagestan and southwestern Astrakhan Oblast.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Caucasus Mountains
text: The Caucasus mountain range is one of the largest mountain ranges in Russia. The tallest mountain in Russia, Mount Elbrus, can be found on the border of the Kabardino-Balkarian Republic and Karachay-Cherkessia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Kamchatka
text: The Kamchatka peninsula has unique grey gravelly soil, as well as the largest number of volcanoes of any region in Russia. They are frequently seen across the peninsula, and in some places can appear quite close such as in Klyuchi.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Far North
text: The landscape in the far north can be recognised by the relatively flat landscape, with very low vegetation.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Dagestan Fields
text: Grassy fields, with bushy vegetation, in early spring Generation 4 coverage is typical for Dagestan. The landscape can either be completely flat or mountainous.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Caspian Sea Area
text: The area west of the Caspian Sea can often be recognised by its extremely dry and flat landscape, especially in Kalmykia, Astrakhan Oblast, and Dagestan.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Murmansk Area
text: An open, hilly landscape with low shrubbery and fireweed usually indicates Murmansk. The lower the shrubbery, the more north it generally is.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Vegetation: Vladivostok Area
text: Lush and diverse forests in a hilly landscape characterises the noticeably warmer region around Vladivostok. Most of the coverage is overcast and has a white car with a long antenna. Further south, near the tri-border, you will find a more open rolling hill landscape.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Olkhon Island
text: Olkhon Island on Lake Baikal has a single road, driving on rolling sandy hills during sunset. You can often see Lake Baikal directly with a mountain ridge across the bay.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Kolyma Highway
text: The eastern half of the Kolyma Highway going to Magadan features a lot of tall hills and mountains, usually shrouded in a haze. Most of the roads are unpaved and feature dark gravelly soil. The haze is not present in the western half.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Coverage: Omsk
text: The coverage in Omsk Oblast is some of the most recognizable in Russia. It is typically summer Generation 4 and has a distinct landscape consisting of green agricultural fields, which are interrupted by isolated patches of (primarily) birch forest. Note that in Generation 3, this landscape can be seen in a much larger area of Russia.

credit.licence: Learnable Meta; notes partly from Plonk It (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

clues.title: Landscape: Tunkinsky National Park

clues.title: Plate: Russia
text: Russian licence plates are fully white with black text.
NOTE: Most European counterparts will feature a blue strip on the left hand side.

clues.title: Street sign: Moscow street sign
text: Moscow street signs are blue with white text, their bigger than any other russian city street sign and are commonly spread throughout the city. The house numbers are also as big and sometimes the street signs can have different shapes.

clues.title: Street sign: St Petersburg street sign
text: St. Petersburg street signs include a transliteration of the street name on a black background with a unique logo on top with fancy borders. There is always another sign under it with a number written on in. They are primarily found downtown.

clues.title: Language: Russian
text: Russian is an East Slavic language related to Ukrainian and Belarusian. Russian uses the Cyrillic script, and contains the special letters **Ы**, **Э**, **Ё** and **Ъ**. **Ё** is also used in Mongolian and **Ъ** is used in Bulgarian (where it's more common).

The Russian word for street is **улица** (ulitsa), sometimes abbreviated **ул.** (ul.). Most other Slavic languages also use **улица**/**ulica**. The Ukrainian word however is **вулиця** (vulytsya), abbreviated **вул.** (vul.).
The Russian word for city is **город** (gorod), abbreviated **г.** (g.). The Ukrainian word is instead **місто** (misto), abbreviated **м.** (m.).
